Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Hospitals, Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please press star one if you'd like to register for a question. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Hospitals, Inc.'s financial results for the third quarter. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Patel, Chief Medical Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency across our 45-hospital footprint and growing outpatient facilities.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on five key aspects: net patient revenue growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, operating margin performance by segment, revenue per admission trends and drivers, our payer revenue mix including percentages from Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and self-pay, and the impact of our cost reduction initiatives.

On net patient revenue, we saw strong growth reflecting our focus on high-acuity outpatient services and payer optimizations. Operating margins expanded across segments, particularly in ambulatory services. Revenue per admission trended upward due to case mix improvements and ancillary capture. Our payer mix remained stable with Medicare leading, and cost initiatives delivered substantial savings.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael, and good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.47 billion, an increase of 8.7% compared to the same period last year and 3.2% quarter-over-quarter from $2.39 billion in Q2. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, improved case mix, and outpatient momentum, even amid reimbursement challenges and economic pressures.

Let me dive deeper into net patient revenue performance. On a same-facility basis—excluding our recent acquisition of three facilities in the Southeast—net patient revenue grew 2.8% quarter-over-quarter and 7.9% year-over-year. Adjusted patient admissions rose 1.5% sequentially and 4.2% annually, powered by a 6% surge in elective procedures such as orthopedics and cardiology interventions, now operating at 105% of pre-pandemic levels. Our case mix index climbed to 1.68 from 1.65 in the prior quarter and 1.62 a year ago, signaling a shift to higher-reimbursed DRGs, especially complex cardiac and neuro cases.

Outpatient revenue shone brightly, making up 58% of total net patient service revenue—up from 55% last quarter—and expanding 5.1% quarter-over-quarter and 12.3% year-over-year to $1.43 billion. This mirrors trends at peers like HCA Healthcare and Tenet, with ambulatory surgery centers and hospital outpatient departments gaining share from physician offices despite CMS site-neutral payment pressures. Our over 120 outpatient facilities, enhanced by the ApexOne platform—a proprietary tech integrating Epic MyChart with AI scheduling—lifted observation stays by 3% and infusion therapy volumes by 7%, notably oncology under value-based deals with UnitedHealthcare.

Inpatient revenue reached $1.04 billion, up 1.1% quarter-over-quarter and 4.8% year-over-year, moderated by average length of stay dipping to 4.7 days from 4.8 as we optimize throughput following Q1 staffing builds. Patient days held flat sequentially but rose 3.1% annually, with behavioral health beds—15% of licensed capacity—growing 9% amid the mental health surge.

Payer mix stayed steady: Medicare at 42% of net revenue, Medicaid 18%, commercial and managed care 35%, self-pay and other 5%. Commercial pricing per admission increased 4.2% year-over-year, surpassing Medicare's 2.1% rise, due to FY24 renegotiations with Blue Cross Blue Shield in Sunbelt markets like Florida, Texas, and Arizona, securing 5-7% uplifts on fee-for-service rates. Medicaid redeterminations post-pandemic have hit low-acuity volumes in Georgia and North Carolina, contracting net revenue per day by 150 basis points.

On deductions, net revenue retention improved to 92.4% from 91.8%, thanks to ClaimGuard AI, which cut initial denial rates 18% via predictive coding audits during our 85% complete Cerner-to-Epic migration. Bad debt as a percentage of gross revenue eased to 2.1% from 2.3%, supported by expanded charity care aligned with the Hospital Price Transparency Rule—totaling $85 million, up slightly year-over-year from community health assessments in rural Texas. Our Sunbelt division, 65% of revenue, grew 10.2% annually on 2.5% population gains and joint replacement demand, while Midwest markets rose 5.4% despite Humana Medicare Advantage adjustments. This diversification shields us from coastal labor issues.

These results affirm our Outpatient First strategy, with $250 million in 15 new ASCs targeting 20% EBITDA margins versus inpatient's 12%. We're piloting ortho bundles with Aetna for 15% readmission upside via Encompass Health partnerships. For Q4, we guide 7-9% year-over-year net patient revenue growth, CMI at 1.67-1.70, watching CMS's proposed 2.9% IPPS cut and prior auth delays. This sets us for full-year $9.8-10.0 billion in net patient revenue, with 50 basis point margin expansion.

Turning to operating margins by segment, our consolidated figure hit 12.4%, up 110 basis points year-over-year, fueled by high-margin outpatient growth and cost discipline amid labor inflation, supply pressures, and payer shifts. Refer to page 14 of our earnings deck.

Acute Care Hospitals, 68% of revenues at $2.8 billion, achieved 10.2% margins—150 basis points better than last year. Adjusted admissions grew 4.2%, CMI to 1.68 from 1.62, strong in orthopedics, cardiology, neurosurgery. Revenue per adjusted admission rose 5.1% to $14,200 on IPPS Medicare hikes and commercial mix to 42% from 39%. Labor rose just 3.8% via AMN partnerships and AI scheduling cutting overtime 22%. Supplies improved 40 basis points to 18.5% through Vizient GPO deals on implants and pharma. Southeast facilities hit 11.8% margins on population and tourism electives; Midwest at 9.1% from Medicaid redeterminations. Value-based ACO REACH covers 28% of Medicare lives, adding 25 basis points.

Ambulatory Surgery Centers and Outpatient, 18% at $740 million, posted 22.7% margins, up 220 basis points. Volumes up 12% to 145,000 cases across 42 ASCs, including Texas tuck-ins. Revenue per case up 7.3% to $5,100 on bundles and site shifts—35% of system ortho/GI here. Anesthesia supplies down 15% via Cardinal Health, Epic MyChart cut no-shows 18%. West Coast at 25.1%, East Coast 20.8%. Targeting 25%+ with pain and endoscopy.

Post-Acute Care, 9% at $370 million, margins steady at 14.8%. Revenues up 6% on 88% occupancy, 5% skilled nursing days. Medicare to 52% from 49% on 2.9% SNF PPS. Contract labor and therapy up 4.5%, offset by in-house academies reducing agency 30%. Northeast at 16.2%, Texas 13.1% post-hurricanes. Divesting two IRFs for high-acuity SNFs.

Physician Services, 5% at $205 million, margins to 8.9%, up 90 basis points. Revenues up 9% on 9,200 wRVUs per provider. Value-based pods cover 45% lives, $12 million savings. Southwest 10.4%, Midwest 7.2%. Epic Caboodle hits 96% coding accuracy.

In sum, outpatient at 40% mix drives 13%+ FY24 consolidated margins, outpacing HCA.

Next, revenue per admission—or RPA, net patient revenue over admissions—stood at $16,450, up 6.2% year-over-year and 1.8% sequentially. First half 2024 averaged $16,320, beating HCA's 4.9% and Tenet's 3.8% per Kaufman Hall.

Drivers: CMI up 2.4% to 1.92 from 1.84, via 12% surgical cardiac like TAVR/CABG, 8% oncology with Guardant. CDI with Nuance AI and 3M captured $28 million extra on HCC/SOI/ROM—up 15%.

Payer shifts added 2.8 points: commercial to 47% from 43%, rates up 7.1% to $22,400 vs. Medicare's 0.2% to $13,200. Medicaid at 18% dragged 0.5 points on redeterminations, offset by $15 million ACO REACH savings.

Ancillary at 42% of RPA from 39%: IR up 18% with GE AI CT, pharmacy to $1,850 via Omnicell 340B, behavioral 14% admissions with 15% premiums.

Southeast RPA up 7.5% to $17,200 on MA 32% mix, Florida Medicaid +5.2%; Midwest 3.1% to $15,600 on bad debt. Epic upgrade hit 97.5% clean claims, A/R to 42 days; AI coding cut denials 22%. Net of variables: $4,620, up 420 basis points via CareRev.

Guide Q3 RPA $16,600-16,800, FY 5-6% on M&A, HealthBridge Direct tele-care. Risks: CMS MS-DRG cuts, MA scrutiny.

On payer mix: Medicare 48%, up 150 basis points; Medicaid 18% flat; commercial/managed 28%, down from 29%; self-pay/other 6%. Average per adjusted day $2,450, up 3.2% on CMI 1.68.

Medicare growth from boomers, MA to 42% with United/Humana; acuity beds, Epic MyChart boosted CMI 2.5%, offset OPPS drug trim via 340B $12 million.

Medicaid steady on CA expansion, 4% days up; Midwest softer. State payments for behavioral/OB, AI prior auth cut denials 22%, 97% collections in 60 days.

Commercial dip on Anthem/Cigna, per case to $14,200 from No Surprises; bundles for ortho/maternity, employer-direct pursuits.

Self-pay bad debt to 2.1% from 2.8% via charity, LexisNexis screening, CareCredit—AR to 45 days. Southeast Medicare 52%, West Medicaid 24%.

Strategy: MA VBC to 50% by 2025 with Devoted; commercial +100-200 bps via analytics; self-pay sub-4% bad debt on 3M coding. 4-5% reimbursement growth FY25.

Operating expenses were $2.16 billion, representing 87.6% of net revenue. We focused on costs while investing in growth.

Our cost reduction initiatives yielded $185 million run-rate savings year-to-date, beating $150 million target by 23%, lifting EBITDA margins 210 basis points to 14.8% from 12.7%.

Supply chain: $72 million (39%) via Vizient/HealthTrust—11% cuts on implants/contrast, Oracle AI inventory down 18% costs/25% write-offs. Midwest supplies per APD to $1,225 from $1,420.

Labor: $64 million (35%)—agency RN to 4% from 12%, AMN upskilling retention to 87%; Cerner analytics LOS to 4.6 days. Urban labor per APD down 8.7%, rural 12%.

Admin/tech: $49 million (26%)—UiPath RPA automates 65% prior auth/denials, AR to 45 days; divest CA centers, tele-ICU 28% visits cut opex 16%. VBC 35% revenue, HCC +7%.

Opex per APD down 6.8%, non-labor 9.2%; FCF $320 million up 42%. Urban margins to 16.5%, rural 11.2%. FY24 $220-240 million savings, Precision AI pilot readmissions -10-15%. EPS 5-7% growth.

Net income was $285 million, or $1.42 per share. We're on track for annual goals.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our value-based care programs have shown promising results, with a 15% reduction in readmission rates through enhanced post-acute coordination. We are also focused on leveraging technology like AI-driven predictive analytics and Epic integrations to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination across our continuum.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Emily. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the impact of the ApexOne platform on your revenue growth and its impact on hospital efficiency?

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Good morning, David. The ApexOne platform has been transformative. It's integrated Epic MyChart with AI scheduling, driving 3% higher observation stays and 7% infusion volumes, contributing roughly 2 points to our outpatient revenue growth this quarter. On efficiency, it's reduced no-shows by 18% and optimized throughput, supporting our LOS improvements and overall 1.5% admission growth. We're scaling it network-wide next year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jennifer Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Kim:
What are your plans for expanding your network of hospitals and clinics in the coming year?

Tom Hargrove:
Thanks, Jennifer. We're targeting 5-7 new ASCs and two micro-hospitals in high-growth Sunbelt areas like Texas and Florida, backed by our $250 million M&A pipeline. This builds on our recent Southeast tuck-ins, focusing on high-CMI assets to boost RPA and margins. We'll prioritize outpatient to hit 20% EBITDA there, while consolidating underperformers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Torres with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Mark Torres:
Can you elaborate on the specific technologies you are implementing to improve care coordination?

Dr. Emily Patel:
Certainly, Mark. Key is our Epic Caboodle analytics for 96% coding accuracy and real-time bed management, plus Nuance Dragon Medical One for CDI capturing $28 million extra. We've rolled out GE Revolution Apex CT for IR and Philips tele-ICU, now 28% of visits, slashing readmissions 15%. Cerner Revenue Cycle AI cuts denials 22%, tying into value-based ACO REACH for shared savings.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Rachel Patel:
Thanks. On cost initiatives, how sustainable are the labor savings with ongoing shortages, and any update on supply chain?

Lisa Chen:
Great question, Rachel. Labor savings are sustainable via our Core Staffing Model—agency at 4%, retention 87% with AMN academies, and Cerner predictive scheduling. We've seen 8.7% per APD cuts in urban areas. Supplies: 11% reductions locked in via Vizient, Oracle AI inventory efficiencies persisting. Run-rate to $220-240 million FY24, with upside from tele-care.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Hospitals, Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
